name: ptrace-traceme
why: ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME, a0=0) is the anti-debug self-trace this rule anchors on
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for ptrace_traceme_behavioral.c's TRACEME record

name: ptrace-traceme-packer
why: a packed/obfuscated binary self-tracing to block a debugger is the same primitive from a different process
source: synthetic: a packed binary issuing PTRACE_TRACEME

name: ptrace-attach
why: ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, a0=0x10) is process injection, not self-trace; the rule description distinguishes the two, so the a0=0 request must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: a debugger/injector attaching to another process

name: ptrace-cont
why: ptrace(PTRACE_CONT, a0=7) is what the atomic's parent tracer issues to resume the child; it is not a TRACEME and must not fire
source: synthetic: the parent tracer's PTRACE_CONT in the ptrace atomic

name: tcgets-ioctl-on-stdin
why: auditd logs ptrace()'s a0 as the request, but for ioctl() a0 is the fd number; ioctl(0, TCGETS) on stdin (what every interactive shell issues at startup) holds the a0=0 atom yet is not the ptrace syscall. This is the realistic high-volume look-alike in this schema, so the ptrace syscall anchor must be load-bearing
source: recorded: strace of an interactive bash on a pty -- ioctl(0, TCGETS=0x5401) = 0

name: close-noise
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor

name: gdb-inferior-traceme-filtered
why: `gdb ./prog` forks the inferior, which calls ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME) before exec with gdb's comm and exe; the gdb entry of debugger_images suppresses it (the old rule fired on it)
source: gdb/inf-ptrace.c inf_ptrace_me(): ptrace(PT_TRACE_ME, 0, 0, 0) in the forked child; events as in the benign corpus gdb template

name: gdbserver-inferior-traceme-filtered
why: `gdbserver :port ./prog` forks the inferior, which calls PTRACE_TRACEME before exec; the gdbserver entry of debugger_images suppresses it
source: gdb/gdbserver/linux-low.c linux_create_inferior: ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME, 0, 0, 0) in the forked child

name: traceme-with-gdb-comm-from-tmp
why: a packed binary that names itself gdb with prctl and self-traces still fires: the gdb entry needs the gdb binary as well as the comm
